cells.tense: You are choosing a direction now, and choosing it as one.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Steady the choice you made when something tugs at it this week. Skip the argument. Keep walking. Notice afterwards which pull it was and what holding cost you.
cells.core:
What you steer by is real feeling, so the direction holds whoever's inside it without you forcing your attention onto it. You feel the way, the way stays steady, and you keep making the call. That's the work of choosing, already doing itself through you.

Something will pull at that course before the week runs out — a mood, a voice, a possibility that looks just as good from here. No need to argue it down or defend the whole course. Hold the line once: stay with what you picked and find out a day later what standing there was like. One refusal, not a campaign. Afterwards the course is yours, and you'll know you chose it.
cells.sheetLine: You choose with feeling, and the choice holds.
cells.verb: Choosing to move as one, with what is around you
cells.place: In the place where you set direction and mean it

cells.tense: You will be watching for the next thing that could break this apart.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Stop working on something your care already built — a routine, an agreement, a plan that works. Leave it be and look at what is there. Find out what pressing on it was costing.
cells.core:
A course is chosen, and your attention keeps sweeping it for weak spots — who might drift off, which part isn't settled yet. The bracing is a second job, and it's the one eating the week. You're overseeing a future for something already standing.

Your care has brought this one somewhere. Let one part of it sit in view and do nothing to it. Then look at what's there and count what it took to build. The energy that comes back belongs to the direction itself, and you'll find you still want it once resting stops costing you. What grew from care doesn't need you standing over it to stay standing.

cells.tense: You chose a direction once, and you are still standing where you chose it.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Take what's pulling at your time right now and put a name on whose it is. Then hand one back that isn't yours, and give an hour to something you actually chose.
cells.core:
The direction was picked and hasn't been moved since. Now there's a set of other people's wants and old duties around you, and you keep handling them because handling is easier than choosing. Somewhere in there is a course nobody consulted for a while. That isn't failure — it's an arrangement that got handled.

Re-deciding the whole thing isn't the ask. Sort the pulls: the ones genuinely yours, and the ones inherited and unchecked. Some will name themselves once they sit next to each other. Give one that's yours a plain hour, and tell nobody you did. The hour shows you what choosing feels like from your own seat again.

cells.tense: You are steering this course already, and you would not say so.
cells.act: give directions plainly, once, and let them walk
cells.ask: Catch one turn you made lately — a choice of yours that shifted things for someone else. Give it its plain description, once, to yourself. Then get back to walking.
cells.core:
Along this course you keep making the calls. You see where it turns, you set the next stretch, and then you file it under timing, or under something that simply needed doing. The steering is real and it is happening. What's out of place is that your name isn't on it.

Next time you notice yourself making one of those calls, pause long enough to name it plainly, once, before you move on. No speech — one true sentence to yourself, and no audience for it. Then keep walking. When you know the course was set by you, you can set it where you meant it to go, and the next stretch stops being something that simply happened to the room.
